sources.evidence: January 2026 OMR release uses an AddressBase Premium premises base filtered to postal and non-demolished premises
sources.guard: BDUK current/future flags are not retail orderability and are not directly comparable with Ofcom because premises bases, respondents, methods and reference dates differ.

sources.evidence: The official publication provides an HTML technical note and a 174 KB sample CSV for England and Wales.
sources.guard: The sample is schema evidence only and cannot be extrapolated into national row counts, parcel coverage or serviceability.

sources.evidence: The July 2026 release is a 16 July snapshot
sources.guard: Monthly contract progress is rounded, may omit deferred scope and must not be used to assess contractual milestones or parcel-level orderability.

sources.evidence: The January 2026 release distinguishes contract delivery tracking from official statistics on connections resulting from BDUK subsidy.
sources.guard: Historical rounded contract totals cannot replace a current UPRN record and are not directly comparable with official-statistics delivery measures.

sources.evidence: The Spring 2026 publication lists the January 2026 fixed broadband archive as a 32.2 MB download and separates fixed coverage from mobile data.
sources.guard: Publication metadata does not replace ZIP-byte, corrected-file, schema and 1,741,096-row runtime validation.

sources.evidence: Ofcom states broadband checker availability and predicted speeds are based on data supplied by major UK internet service providers.
sources.guard: Checker values are predictions and availability indications, not evidence of installation, retail order acceptance or a legal parcel relationship.

sources.evidence: OS Open UPRN contains the UPRN and position for included AddressBase Premium records and is intended for linking datasets by identifier or point.
sources.guard: A point is not a title boundary

sources.evidence: The product provides authoritative UPRN, USRN and TOID relationships, updates every six weeks and contains no geometry.
sources.guard: Authoritative identifier relationships still require version/confidence checks and do not establish title ownership or broadband availability.

sources.evidence: The download contains 11 relationship ZIP packages, each with CSV relationship data, JSON version metadata, licence text and documentation.
sources.guard: Package presence and naming must be validated per relationship

sources.evidence: CSV rows include relationship ID, both identifiers, optional version numbers/dates and a mandatory confidence value.
sources.guard: NULL optional versions and changed or potentially changed confidence values must block silent promotion of a relationship.

sources.evidence: Each relationship package includes JSON metadata with filename, publication date, epoch name and source-product metadata.
sources.guard: Every imported relation must retain package filename, publication date, epoch and source product

sources.evidence: OS Open TOID carries mandatory TOID, version date and source-product attributes, with version number optional.
sources.guard: A TOID can represent many real-world feature types and its generalised location or identifier cannot be assumed to be a building parcel.

sources.evidence: NSUL and ONSUD are six-weekly GB products that allocate UPRNs to statistical geographies using point-in-polygon or OA best-fit methods.
sources.guard: Statistical geography allocation is not an address lifecycle, legal boundary or broadband serviceability determination.

sources.evidence: ONS confirms NSUL/ONSUD are not address products and publishes only postcodes that pass Code-Point Open licensing checks
sources.guard: Retain the stated AddressBase and Code-Point Open epochs

sources.evidence: ONSPD links current and terminated postcodes to geographies using point-in-polygon
sources.guard: A postcode geography is a centroid/mean-point allocation and cannot bind every address in the postcode to one parcel or coverage result.

sources.evidence: A small-user unit postcode can contain many addresses, and a large building may have more than one unit postcode.
sources.guard: Postcode equality is insufficient for unit-level matching

sources.evidence: ONS UPRN products are under OGL with required OS, Royal Mail, GeoPlace and ONS attribution statements.
sources.guard: Licence and third-party attribution metadata must travel with derived records

sources.evidence: ONS Open Geography provides free downloads and metadata, generally under OGL while warning that third-party rights can add conditions.
sources.guard: Portal availability and metadata are discovery evidence only
